name: Extreme heat
summary: Bureau of Meteorology heatwave warning for northern Queensland on 9 Nov; severe to extreme areas contracting north
state: The Bureau of Meteorology's Queensland heatwave warning issued on 9 Nov forecast maximums in the high 30s to low 40s°C inland and on western Cape York, with severe to extreme conditions gradually contracting towards the north of the warning area over the week (WillyWeather, citing BoM). Earlier warnings on 4 Nov reached extreme level in the Kimberley and parts of the Northern Territory (IQAir). This meets the regional-warning line for Watch; no deadly heatwave with top-tier warnings over a large population was found as of 10 Nov.
for_you: People in northern Australia, especially older adults, outdoor workers and remote communities, are most exposed. Follow Bureau of Meteorology warnings and state health advice on staying cool.
rubric_hit: Severe-to-extreme heatwave warnings across northern Australia (BoM, 9 Nov): Watch

why: Heat is the deadliest weather hazard globally, straining power grids, crops and health systems.
drivers: Heat domes, climate warming, season, humidity, urban heat islands.

rubric.alert: Deadly heatwave with top-tier official warnings across a large population.
rubric.watch: Heatwave warnings across a major region, or national temperature records.
rubric.normal: No major heatwaves affecting large populations.
